children: SKYX Platforms plans to merge with Deako in a deal that would combine two players in the smart-home technology industry.

Under the deal, SKYX plans to issue about 18% of its common stock as consideration, subject to up to a two-year lockup and leak out agreement, the companies said Thursday. SKYX would also pay Deako's lender $4 million by closing and issue an $8.5 million note, with about $2.3 million paid in the first quarter of 2027 and the remaining in the fourth quarter of 2027.
After the close of the deal, current SKYX shareholders would own 84% of the combined company, while Deako's shareholders and lender would collectively own 16%.

SKYX said the deal would expand its patent portfolio, bringing on Deako's 20 patents and pending patent applications for plug and play advanced, smart home and AI-activated lighting wall switches. The deal would also grow SKYX's product offerings for the builder, hotel and pro markets, the companies said.
For Deako, the merger would open the door for its products to get involved in SKYX's projects including Marriott and European hotels, the companies said.
Under the deal, Deako's Founder and Chief Executive Derek Richardson would remain CEO of Deako and lead SKYX's growth including to the builder, hotel and pro markets.
